title: Cloudflare's new PQ GeoKey Manager: keys that can only unwrap inside a chosen region, wrapped with hybrid ML-KEM + X25519
description: Cloudflare has introduced a post-quantum (PQ) GeoKey Manager that restricts decryption keys to be unwrapped only within designated geographic regions. This system uses hybrid post-quantum cryptography (ML-KEM-768 plus X25519) to protect keys, ensuring that regional root keys never leave their authorized regions and are stored only in volatile kernel memory on authorized edge servers. The GeoKey Manager supports data sovereignty by enforcing geographic boundaries on key usage, preventing decryption outside the chosen region. It is currently in closed beta with general availability planned for Q1 2027.

aiSummary: Cloudflare's PQ GeoKey Manager is a geographically restricted key management system designed to enforce data sovereignty by allowing decryption keys to be unwrapped only within specified geographic regions. It uses hybrid post-quantum cryptography combining ML-KEM-768 (a NIST standard) and X25519 to secure wrapped keys. The system separates globally distributed wrapped private keys from regional root keys, which are provisioned only to authorized edge servers within the allowed region and stored in volatile kernel keyring memory. Requests attempting to decrypt keys outside their authorized region fail closed, ensuring strict geographic enforcement. The system supports multiple services and epochs, with application-specific keys derived from regional root keys. This approach mitigates 'harvest now, decrypt later' attacks by protecting keys against future quantum computer threats while maintaining high availability and compliance with data localization regulations.
aiImpact: The PQ GeoKey Manager enhances data sovereignty and security by ensuring that decryption keys cannot be unwrapped or used outside authorized geographic regions. This prevents unauthorized access to sensitive data in transit or at rest across Cloudflare's global network. The use of hybrid post-quantum cryptography protects against future quantum computing attacks that could compromise classical encryption. The system's fail-closed behavior on out-of-region decryption attempts reduces the risk of data leakage. However, it introduces operational complexity in managing regional root keys and ensuring correct regional configurations. There are no known exploits in the wild at this time.
